chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Patsy, the daughter who dances and choreographs
summary: Howard says his stepdaughter dances and sings; Mrs. Howard says Patsy assisted Leroy Prinz at the studios and began at sixteen at the Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, there's something here that I'm passing by, and I don't want to pass it by. I know I saw my daughter come in here just now.
Yeah.
She can dance like nobody's business.
Yeah?
And she can sing. She knows all the pieces, everything that you can think about. But she's never said nothing about it. Never tried (inaudible).
I knew she was a dancer. I never
realized she sang.
She was the leader of --
(Unintelligible) We're talking about you.
Yeah, we're getting everybody on here.
Leroy Pring was -- the leader (inaudible) assistant choreographer, out at the studios.
Patsy was the assistant?
Was --
To Leroy Pring?
Uh-huh. She was his assistant.
I saw her name in the ads and in the stories that you showed me in the papers, the whole family was in show business.
So Patsy started when she was quite young then, I guess because of you two.
Yeah, she -- I think she was 16 when she first started with (unintelligible) at the Cotton Club.
Did Patsy work with Jump for Joy?
Yes, yes.
We might get her (inaudible) on here, too, to tell us what she remembers from 'Jump for Joy,' if she'd like to.
Can we get Patsy in here in person? Patsy? Where'd she go?
I think she's in the bath now.
Okay, we'll see.
I think she --
Because, yeah, that was (inaudible), in that too.
I think she --
I don't know.
Who was the choreographer for 'Jump for Joy'? I think she assisted in some stage --
I bet she did. It comes to mind, because Patsy was doing (inaudible) that period so much.
Yeah.
Just about everything that was happening with Patsy Howard was -- bang, producing and doing all kinds of things.
